canonical_statement: Reality is fundamentally dualistic, consisting of independent and dependent principles.

attributions.surface_quote: He believed in the duality of ultimate principles, which he named the independent and the dependent.

canonical_statement: The phenomenal world is a manifestation of the divine will, rather than an independent illusion.

attributions.surface_quote: Maya is only the will of the Lord.

canonical_statement: The material universe is a direct manifestation originating from the body of the Supreme Being.

attributions.surface_quote: The whole world was manifest from the body of Visnu.

canonical_statement: The individual human body serves as a vessel for a spark of the Supreme Spirit.

attributions.surface_quote: The body in which there lives a spark of the Supreme Spirit.

canonical_statement: The universe undergoes cyclical processes of evolution and involution originating from the Supreme Being.

attributions.surface_quote: The creation of the world was by a process of evolution and involution.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality (Krsna) is characterized by a total absence of qualities (nirguna).

attributions.surface_quote: Vallabha held that Krsna was devoid of all qualities

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality, Brahman, is composed of the triad of existence, intelligence, and bliss.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is sat, cit, and ananda.

canonical_statement: The manifestation of the universe occurs through the evolution and involution of the properties inherent in Brahman.

attributions.surface_quote: evolution (avirbhava) and involution (tirobhava) of its properties.

canonical_statement: Ignorance (avidya) is not a positive reality but a negation or obscuration of true knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: Avidya is decidedly not a reality; it is only the negation of vidya.

canonical_statement: The individual's divine spiritual nature is inherently present but obscured by limiting conditions (upadhis).

attributions.surface_quote: our godly nature, our spiritual principle, hidden by the upadhis.

canonical_statement: The individual soul and Brahman are ontologically identical; their apparent differentiation is caused solely by limiting adjuncts (upadhis).

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman becomes the individual soul only by upadhis, i.e., self-imposed limitations.

canonical_statement: Ignorance (avidya) has no positive existence and cannot fundamentally alter or conceal the essential self-luminosity of Brahman.

attributions.surface_quote: Maya is merely negative. It has no positive existence to be able to conceal anything.

canonical_statement: The perception of reality is mediated and constrained by intellectual forms such as time, space, and causality.

attributions.surface_quote: Between that and ourselves are the intellectual forms of Time, Space, and Causality.

canonical_statement: The nature of any entity must be categorized as either real or unreal.

attributions.surface_quote: it must either have the nature of reality or of unreality

canonical_statement: Maya is neither absolutely real nor absolutely unreal.

attributions.surface_quote: we do not admit the reality of Maya, but at the same time we do not hold that it is unreal

canonical_statement: The world possesses empirical existence while lacking ultimate reality.

attributions.surface_quote: Empirically the world is, but it is not sat

canonical_statement: Inquiring into the causal origin of Maya is a category error.

attributions.surface_quote: The question as to what is the cause of Maya is... an illegitimate one

canonical_statement: Causality is a structural law limited to the phenomenal world and cannot be applied to the origin of the phenomenal world itself.

attributions.surface_quote: Causality is the general law in the world... but it has no warrant to transcend itself.

canonical_statement: The attribution of independent reality to Maya creates a dualism that renders the explanation of the phenomenal world logically impossible.

attributions.surface_quote: The moment we grant a real existence to Maya, our whole theory falls with it.

canonical_statement: Maya is ontologically indeterminate, being neither strictly existent (sat) nor non-existent (asat).

attributions.surface_quote: Maya is anirvacaniya, i.e., incapable of definition, because it is neither an entity nor a non-entity.

canonical_statement: The Atman is the sole reality, serving as the standard against which the non-reality of Maya is measured.

attributions.surface_quote: It is not sat, since the Atman alone is real.

canonical_statement: The phenomenal world and the sense of individual identity are products of an erroneous superimposition of objective attributes onto the Self.

attributions.surface_quote: erroneous transfer of the things and relations of the objective world to the Self

canonical_statement: The individual is in essence identical to the Absolute Spirit, despite the subjective experience of separation.

attributions.surface_quote: we are in reality no other than the Absolute Spirit

canonical_statement: The perception of a real, separate world is a manifestation of ignorance (avidya) rather than an ontological reality.

attributions.surface_quote: clash between our knowledge and feelings... is due to our ignorance

canonical_statement: The Absolute is fundamentally devoid of attributes, as the imposition of qualities necessitates limitation and contradicts the nature of the infinite.

attributions.surface_quote: The ultimate truth remains without attributes; to impose attributes makes the Absolute non-absolute.

canonical_statement: The universe functions as the physical body of the Divine, which acts as the animating soul of all existence.

attributions.surface_quote: The universe is the body of which Brahman is the soul.

canonical_statement: Metaphysical knowledge is hierarchical, divided into lower knowledge of a qualified deity and higher knowledge of the attributeless Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: Passages speaking of qualified Brahman are Apara vidya, while Para includes metaphysical truth as it is.

canonical_statement: The Absolute exists simultaneously as God, individual soul, and material reality.

attributions.surface_quote: He is Himself all the three entities: God, soul and matter.

canonical_statement: The individual soul is ontologically identical to the Universal Absolute.

attributions.surface_quote: Tat tvam asi denotes the oneness of the individual with the Universal.

canonical_statement: The Absolute is identical to pure consciousness, rendering the concept of 'knowledge of Brahman' a category error.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman is itself knowledge, the term being used in the higher sense of pure consciousness.

canonical_statement: Ignorance (Avidya) is an illusory state that is inherently negated by the presence of pure consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: Avidya being like darkness is itself expelled when light comes in.

canonical_statement: The differentiation between the subject, the act of knowing, and the object is an illusory construct.

attributions.surface_quote: The differentiation between the knower, knowledge, and the known is unreal.

canonical_statement: Empirical reality and the laws of karma are valid only within the phenomenal realm and cease to apply upon the realization of Brahman.

attributions.surface_quote: Karma, its determinations, and with it everything else, is supposed to be real, but only so far.

canonical_statement: The Atman is inherently free from the bondage of karma, as such laws do not affect the ultimate nature of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: The laws of Karma are valid within the phenomenal, but in no way do they produce any real knowledge to the Atman.

canonical_statement: Divine grace is a functional concept for the unawakened, but in absolute terms, grace is the identity between two forms of consciousness.

attributions.surface_quote: Grace is only possible when there is a direct and perfect communion... an identity between the two forms of consciousness.

canonical_statement: The distinction between the knower, knowledge, and the known is a fictitious construct of the practical mind, not an absolute truth.

attributions.surface_quote: The differentiation between the knower, knowledge, and the known... the distinction is certainly fictitious in the absolute sense.

canonical_statement: Liberation is achieved solely through the removal of ignorance (avidya) via true knowledge, as deeds and devotion are insufficient.

attributions.surface_quote: Without such a knowledge, mere devotion or deeds will never lead one to the same goal.

canonical_statement: The subject of knowledge (the knower) cannot be known as an object of knowledge.

attributions.surface_quote: By what shall we know the knower?

canonical_statement: The Absolute is impersonal in nature, yet this impersonality encompasses the true essence of personality.

attributions.surface_quote: The impersonal conception of the Absolute is truly personal.

canonical_statement: The individual soul (Jiva) is ontologically distinct and separate from the ultimate reality (Brahman).

attributions.surface_quote: The Jiva, being limited, is distinct from Brahman.

canonical_statement: The universe and the individual self are identical to the Absolute, rendering distinctions illusory.

attributions.surface_quote: I am Brahman, and all this universe is Brahman.

canonical_statement: The ontological unreality of the phenomenal world is compatible with its functional validity within the framework of empirical experience.

attributions.surface_quote: unreality of the world does not deprive it of its empiric reality

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality (Brahman) is purely conscious and cannot be inherently united with non-conscious matter.

attributions.surface_quote: Brahman, which is all cit, should be in inseparable union with acit.

canonical_statement: The manifestation of the world from a non-intelligent cause requires an intelligent principle to initiate activity.

attributions.surface_quote: Activity... in every case it results from an intelligent principle.

canonical_statement: Non-intelligent matter lacks the capacity for spontaneous, orderly evolution into complex forms.

attributions.surface_quote: Pradhana cannot evolve itself spontaneously into multiform modifications.

canonical_statement: The ultimate reality, Brahman, is non-dual and inherently devoid of motion or change.

attributions.surface_quote: consequence of the non-duality of Brahman no motion is possible

canonical_statement: The appearance of motion and causality in the world is a fictitious construct derived from Maya and Avidya.

attributions.surface_quote: Lord being fictitiously connected with Maya, which consists of name and form presented by Avidya

canonical_statement: The concept of causality is ultimately untenable when applied to the nature of Brahman as the cause of the world.

attributions.surface_quote: this conception of causality is not tenable

canonical_statement: The Absolute (Brahman) is perceived as phenomenal reality only when categorized by the mind.

attributions.surface_quote: the moment any such category is introduced the Absolute (Brahman) is conceived as Phenomenal

canonical_statement: The doctrine of Maya is fundamentally misunderstood when it is treated as an objective reality.

attributions.surface_quote: All the chief objections to Maya rest upon a misconception, viz., to take it as a reality.

canonical_statement: The relationship between the Absolute and the universe is a central problem in Indian philosophical systems.

attributions.surface_quote: the relation of the Absolute to the Universe.

canonical_statement: The doctrine of Maya serves as a fundamental explanatory framework for the nature of reality within Vedantic philosophy.

attributions.surface_quote: The doctrine of Maya in the philosophy of the Vedanta
